utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I believe you're up next.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. VG-38.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Mr. Milan Lukic. I'm going to ask you some questions today about what you remember back in 1992, and can I do that today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you were a little upset yesterday. Are you okay today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Might I ask you why you'd become so frustrated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether Defence counsel Mr. Alarid wishes to refer to the psychological state of mind of my client or to his state of health. I believe this is the way of intimidating the witness and has nothing to do with what is about to follow, i.e., relevant questions that stem from the examination-in-chief I led.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'm inclined to agree. For my own part, I did not notice. I wasn't aware that the witness was -- was upset. Move on to the matters at hand, the matters of substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I simply wanted to make sure that the witness was in a good state of mind today to testify and that I wouldn't otherwise annoy an annoyed state of mind, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 38, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you grew up in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell the Court a little bit about your childhood before 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to school. I did sports as a boy, football mainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, this tragedy happened when you were how old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fourteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in earlier statements you'd said thirteen and a half and you clarified today. Have you had an opportunity to review your earlier statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I've read some statements, and it could have been a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But today you're sure you were over 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, 14 and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in June of 1992 school was out; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But tensions between Muslims and Serbs had -- had started sometime earlier. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, tell me about how the tension between Muslims and Serbs had started from the perspective of a 14-year-old young boy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you notice as a 14-year-old that things were not good between Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the Uzice Corps arrived in Visegrad I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was that the first time you noticed, or had there been other instances between Muslims and Serbs that may not have been war-like but still were not good?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those were armed people, so we did not feel safe any longer to go to school and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you -- when did school get out that summer? When was the last day of school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I know it was beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was that normal? Was that every year school ended at the beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was different about this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, this year. 1992. I apologise. I'm talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were burnt in a house that year in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I'm more interested backing up a little bit. We'll talk about that -- that evening enough probably for your comfort, but what I'd like to do is go before that and see how things became this that led to that. So in April did your parents keep you out of school early?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only parents. Many Muslims decided not to go to school because they did not feel safe. It was not safe. There were armed people around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before there became these armed people around, how were relations at your school between Muslim children and Serb children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, was your school a mixed school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you have Serb children who were your friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Muslim and Serb children still played together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What happened when the children stopped playing together? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply we did not go to school, and the situation was tense between Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before you stopped going to school were the children acting out any of that tension, or were the kids, at least, okay with Serbs and Muslims playing together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children were not acting out, but the adults were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so your whole childhood was interrupted that spring and summer. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did it upset -- I bet it upset you not to be able to go to school any more because of this tension between Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, please state, the village where you came from, was that a mixed village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before the Uzice Corps came, the fighting started in April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When do you remember the Uzice Corps coming to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 13 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And why do you remember that date so well? I know you've given it in your statements, but why is that burned in your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had calendars, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But sometimes people don't remember an exact date. Sometimes they remember a time. And to remember an exact date, how did you come to remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I can't forget that date when the Uzice Corps arrived and when we were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the Uzice Corps came, how were the relations in your village between your neighbours? That's where it started. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The relations were tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how -- what kind of instances did you see that would display that tension or show the Court that tension?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb neighbours would come to the village and were asking us for weapons, and they attacked us on the 15th of April in Korito [as interpreted] village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so this was two days after the Uzice Corps came to town your neighbours attacked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who attacked you? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local Serbs. The village was divided, but otherwise they were our Serb neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of these neighbours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who are -- who were your neighbours that attacked you? What were their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilija Gavrilovic, Novak Simic, Sretenko Simic, Goran Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the transcript I see that the village of Korito is mentioned. I don't quite see what this means. Maybe it's a typo, I don't know. On page 6, line 2: "Serb neighbours would come to the village and were asking us for weapons, and they attacked us on the 15th of April in the village of Korito."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what is your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That village doesn't exist. It isn't mentioned in the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does that preclude him from saying so if that happened? Where is the village of Korito, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Koritnik is the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it's Koritnik. Yes, Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were interrupted, Mr. 38. What -- what were the names of the neighbours who attacked you? I think you gave us Mr. Gavrilovic, Mr. Simic, and Vasic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was also Dusan Gavrilovic. That's that I have seen. And there were more, but we had hidden in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, was this attack at the same time that you were asked to go to Visegrad and check in with the Red Cross to take a bus and evacuate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 15th of April, and on the 14th of June we were still in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So the first time you were attacked it was just to look for weapons. That was in April; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after the 15th of April were there any more incidents with these neighbours or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they kept coming and asking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How much would they do this to your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only my family. It was the whole village. All the way until we left Koritnik village on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, where was your -- you were a young boy at that time. Where was your father? And you have an older brother too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those of military age were hiding in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that is because the Serbs were taking away boys of military age or men of military age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And these Serbs that were taking them away were these same neighbours who you named earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, since the Uzice Corps was still in Visegrad, those who were coming were mostly Serb neighbours, and of course the troops of the Uzice Corps. They were looking for men of military age.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when the troops of the Uzice Corps would take men of military age, did you hear from them again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so in your mind did the Uzice Corps cause many disappearances amongst your people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in between April 15th and June, were there any more instances with your family that you witnessed directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Between April 15th and June when you left your village, were there any more instances against your family by Serbians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not against my family, no. Up until the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in the 14th of June you were approached or your village was approached by neighbours; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who approached the villagers and told them they had to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Dusan Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know if he -- and this may be a tough question for you to answer from your being 14, but do you know if this man was a member of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before that date you did know Mitar Vasiljevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had seen him from going to school and knowing him from around Visegrad. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know him from school. I used to see him around Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and what I meant was that you would see him probably going to and from school in town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him from the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He worked there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two of my relatives worked there as interns, and sometimes I would go to the swimming pool at the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So before June of 1992, how many times would you say you had been able to see Mr. Vasiljevic in your life? And you don't have to be exact, but give me a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, on -- on my way to school I'd see him I don't know how many times, but I also saw him at the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had you seen him more than a hundred times in your life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: More than a thousand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that you would be able -- you would have been able to identify Mr. Vasiljevic by name and description even if this had not have happened in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had you ever heard of Milan Lukic before June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you'd never seen him before June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You had never seen him before June of 1992. You'd never looked him in the face and said, "That's Milan Lukic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Before June of 1992 or June 14th of 1992, had you ever heard his name mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How had you heard his name mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An individual came who had been taken to I don't know where and who was subsequently brought to the Koritnik village at Vila Jasmina -- that's Vila Jasmina. She was burnt in that house and she knew Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was just before the incident in June of 1992 is what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And other than that, is Milan a common name for boys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In peacetime nobody knew who either Milan or Dragan were, but I wouldn't say that the name itself was uncommon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's what I meant, that it's a common name amongst the community, Milan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that Lukic is a common surname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if all you heard was the name Milan Lukic, you might not know exactly who someone was speaking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's right. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, Witness. The question was: If you heard the name Milan Lukic, you would not necessarily know who the person was. Is that so? That's what the counsel is trying to find out, because you have said it was a common name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Counsel asked you whether the name Milan was common, and you said that it was a common name in the community and you also said that Lukic is a common surname, and so he went on to ask you if you heard the name Milan Lukic, you would not know exactly who that person was speaking about because the name is so common.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the name itself, in peacetime one did not make any distinction between various names, either Milan or Dragan. One did not pay attention to whether one's name was Muslim or Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before June of 1998, you had left your home one time before when the Uzice Corps came into town; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And on the way to the stadium the Muslims from your village were -- their valuables were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Weapons were taken by the troops of the Uzice Corps, and those of military age were taken away. Admittedly not all of them were taken away, but some were, as I was able to see myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's -- maybe you misunderstood me. What I was talking about is when all the Muslims were gathered in the stadium by the Uzice Corps and everyone had to be taken there to the stadium. People's valuables were taken on the way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not state that. I didn't say that. I only know that they took weapons off those who had them and that men of military age were taken away by members of the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recall your statement of November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before that you gave a statement in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you don't recall in your statement of November 1995 that on the way you stayed in the village of Barimo? You stayed overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed overnight at the Barimo village, and we were taken to the stadium in Visegrad. There they were taking weapons off people and were taking away men of military age.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recall stating that on the way to the stadium in the village of Brstanica, "The Chetniks searched us and took gold and jewellery and money and other valuables"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that they were taking weapons, and they were not taking jewellery or money.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can the court officer please put up what's been entered or uploaded as 2D00-0694, which is the English version of the November 6, 1995, statement. And B/C/S version is -- it doesn't appear to be uploaded on my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the Prosecution spent about 55 minutes in examination-in-chief, and that is just about the time you would be getting for cross-examination. You have roughly another 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'd like to get to the point, then. I think that's appropriate given the time constraints. I'd simply like to place into evidence the statements previously mentioned, the 11 August 1995, which is statement which is 1D00-3264. And actually we did upload the November statement, 6 November 1995 which is 1D00-3271 and would we like to have those placed into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, statement number 1D00-3264 will become Exhibit 1D26, and 3271 will become Exhibit 1D27 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, Mr. 38, when you went to the stadium did you listen to the commander that addressed all your people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise his name was Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we were told right there by the soldiers who were there. They told us Colonel Jovanovic was coming, and that's when a helicopter alighted on the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during the time in the stadium Muslims were being mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- or, rather, some individuals were taken away, those of military age. They were not mistreated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Not beaten," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were Muslims being cursed by Serbian soldiers either on the way or in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not at the stadium itself but as they were on their way to the stadium expletives were expressed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did Colonel Jovanovic tell the people that the White Eagles were under his control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so did that make you feel that the White Eagles were an extension of the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you -- let's go to June of 1992 when you were forced from your homes. It was a neighbour that came to you to tell you that you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And his name was again, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Dusan Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long did -- did Dusan take your people? How far did he go with your people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went together with us all the way to the village of Greben.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what happened in Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We waited for the buses to arrive there. As the buses did not arrive, Milorad Lipovac took us over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'm trying to determine how your case is developing, what your case is, but I am of course aware of the defence of alibi which has been specifically pleaded, but are you going further to suggest that the crimes were committed by others, including members of groups like the White Eagles and so on?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, tangentially yes, Your Honour. I'm not saying --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tangentially, Your Honour, I kind of agree with that. I mean, simply there are other suspects. The town was full of various peoples that clearly demonstrate anti-Muslim sentiment all the way from the neighbourhood level throughout. There are military types. Everyone is describing a variety of people, and if there is a misidentification, yet an assumption of an identification, that rumour can become viral, really, and it becomes to a point in time that if we can establish that people were not able to perfectly identify someone combined with the fact that there are other suspects of unknown types, actually, considering the nature of the war, I think it does go to the realm of possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at what time did Mr. Lipovac leave this procession of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at around half past 3.00. That was when we arrived in Visegrad in front of the Red Cross building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, looking out at the -- at the area in front of the Red Cross building, what do you see? How many people are there, how many soldiers, that kind of situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers passing by on trucks, and there were around ten soldiers moving in our immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The hour was 2.30, not 3.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many soldiers did you see in the trucks just generally in that short time that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were around 15 of them on the truck passing through the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were all the soldiers wearing green camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were they all armed with automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were you molested by the soldiers in the square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not by those; by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What others? What did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Novo Rajak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know Novo Rajak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him because a relative of his went to school with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what did Novo tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cursed us while we were there. There was a dog who followed our group, and he told us to -- to tell the dog to go away. He said, "Somebody's going to get bitten," and then he fired at the dog, killing him. Then he ordered that the dog be thrown from the bridge, the old Turkish bridge, Cuprija, into the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who did he order to do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Kurspahic did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Novo Rajak was a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But he did carry some authority right there in the square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At what point in time were you directed to go spend the night, or when did you find out that there were no buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were there for about 45 minutes to an hour. They told us no buses will be arriving, and then they moved us to Mahala, that is to Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what day of the week is this if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was the 14th. I think it was a Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And why would you think it was a Monday? Did something happen on Sunday, since weekends were often different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Sunday they came and told us that we had to leave the village the next day, Monday, and that's what we did. We left early that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why were you sure it was a Sunday that they told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I think we had some sort of calendars with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're sure it was a Sunday, that's all. I'm not trying to be sarcastic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that day was a Sunday, and on Monday we left the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And you say you were escorted to the homes on Pionirska Street at about 3.00 in the afternoon, 3.30?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you say you were escorted by Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be -- isn't it true that no one you would think to be Milan Lukic was present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What about Milan Susnjar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't there either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you knew Milan Susnjar specifically. How did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a neighbour from the village next to ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how far away was your village from his village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how far were both your villages from Visegrad proper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the distance from the centre of Visegrad to my village was four and a half to five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when -- in one of your statements you testified that when your village was originally attacked by your neighbours about 50 people attacked your village and asked for weapons the first time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was Milan Susnjar one of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you knew him as a long-time local resident and neighbour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you went up to the homes there were less people in one home and more people in another. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at what point in time did Mitar return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around 5.00 p.m., 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was Milan Susnjar a professor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in a bakery. He distributed the bread as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at 5.00 p.m. when Mitar returned, you didn't know the men with him other than Milan Susnjar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Sredoje Lukic. I knew Mitar Vasiljevic. I knew Milan Susnjar. I only didn't know Milan Lukic, but there were other people who did know him. They even went to school with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, since the incident of that night, though, you'd probably heard other horrible rumours about Milan Lukic besides what you experienced. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the first time you gave a statement was in 1995. Why did you not come forward sooner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the opportunity, because I was in Srebrenica and then in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But there were investigations by the local authorities going on at that time. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down there people were struggling for their lives. There was a war going on. There was no one with the time or the resources to carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, by the time people were moved from the original two houses into the one house, night had fallen. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in fact you were very tired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when night fell, isn't it true that there was a lot of -- a lot of homes did not have electricity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the -- in the place where they transferred us before setting us on fire there -- there was no electricity, but in Mujo Memic's house there was electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that the man that you knew as Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Susnjar are the ones that came into the house before moving you is what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not alone. There was Milan Lukic there as well, Sredoje Lukic, Milan Susnjar, Mitar Vasiljevic. Before taking us to that other house, they demanded money, jewellery, and we turned it all over to them. We had to. And finally they body searched us. They stripped us naked, in fact, to search us, and there were two men around the house outside. In case anybody threw anything out of the window, they would have killed him. That evening after 10.30, they moved us to Adem Omeragic's house. We were there until --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, let me -- let me pause you for a second. We'll go there, but where I want to focus on is the two men outside were the ones that you believed to be Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Sredoje was inside the house with Milan Susnjar while Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic were outside the house, and the house had windows. They were outside the windows and looking to see if anyone was going to throw anything out of the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What time did it get dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 8.30 p.m. It began to grow dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there were no streetlights outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some places there were streetlights but not where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so the people that you believe -- the person you believed to be Milan Lukic was outside in the dark at the end of this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The light in the house was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was there glass in the windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when a light is on inside and there's a window, does not the window become like a mirror?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a light on outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you believe that Mitar Vasiljevic came back at 10.30?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We saw them, all four of them, drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that Mitar Vasiljevic was in a hospital with broken leg at 10.30 at night on that night, how would that change your perception?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, sir, money turns everything these days. Give me a computer and I'll produce any sort of paper you like, certificating for instance that you had spent five years abed in a hospital in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you if Mitar Vasiljevic proved he was in a hospital to a Court's satisfaction and he was not there, how would that change your perception?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He has given you the answer, Mr. Alarid, and it's for us to make of it what we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: During the travel between the two homes, it was very dark out, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just another five minutes, Mr. Alarid. You've used 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It was cloudy because it had been raining?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So it was a moonless night as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But these people were carrying a flashlight, sir, and the light was on on the house of Jusuf Memic, I mean the light outside was on. And as we were leaving Jusuf Memic's house to go to Omer's house, they were carrying a flashlight. They told us not to put on our shoes but to go out barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you're saying you saw the face of Mitar Vasiljevic who you knew before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see his face, but I saw his hat and the same uniform that I saw on him the first time when he arrived, because I was not allowed to look closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you were not allowed to look closely at any of these men. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My name is Djuro Cepic and I appear here on behalf of Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before I ask -- start my examination, let me first say that I understand the suffering and the pain of all those who were involved in the incident. I would appreciate it if you listen to my questions carefully, think them over, and give me brief answers if possible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, I maintain to you that my client Sredoje Lukic was not in Pionirska Street that day. He was not in Visegrad, and he took no part in that incident. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I further want to suggest that your identification is not reliable. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I suppose you followed in the media the events surrounding the beginning of the trial of Milan and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Which TV station, Hajat [phoen], the state television of Bosnia or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you come here today to make sure that Sredoje Lukic is convicted or perhaps both of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever is guilty should be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I withdraw the objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By bus up to the bus terminal and then through town, walking through town. I don't know if you know Visegrad well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has just given a date, and this may be a problem for security. He is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. For redaction, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will have that redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Twenty-fifth page, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kindly tell me who drove the bus. Who was the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanaskovic is the name. Rade Tanaskovic from Lijeska. There used to be another driver, Burdus. I don't know where he is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where did you get off the bus in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a stop in Mahala, the neighbourhood called Mahala, and to take the bus I had to go to the bus stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did the bus stop in Mahala on the way back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but sometimes I also went to the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I came to learn Visegrad very well. It's kind of illogical for you to go to the bus stop one kilometre further in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I went to the bus stop because I lived in Jelacic village. Bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When did you live in Jelacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did VG-84 go to school with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I went to Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did he attend Vuk Karadzic school with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You described yesterday and repeated it today as well that Mitar Vasiljevic and others came to the house. What I want to know is what they looked like. First would you agree with the description that your mother gave in her statement to the investigators of the ICTY in February, 1998. In her statement of 12 and 13 February, 1998, in the Serbian language, page 5, paragraph 2, and in English page 4, paragraph 3, she describes Sredoje Lukic as a man of 40 years of age or so, dark hair, medium height, and stoutish, and she described Milan Lukic as around 30, perhaps less, tall, neither stout nor thin, and his hair was light brown.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What was the difference in height then between the two of them in centimetres, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much. Five centimetres, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Sredoje have a moustache, the policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was his hair longer by the thickness of one or two fingers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You said he was stout. What kind of stout, like a barrel or simply a stocky man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't really very fat. He had some sort of flak jacket on him, a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You say flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the military vest like bullet-proof vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sredoje did not carry any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were armed with automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So all of them down to the last man were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to automatic rifles they also had grenades and bayonets.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me about Susnjar's appearance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was rather short. He had a moustache. Neither fat nor thin, medium build. He had crop hair, black.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How tall was he compared to Sredoje and Milan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this move between the two houses, where was Sredoje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they were driving us in front of them, they were all outside the house, and they had something like a flashlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did we stay outside the first Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were leaving the house they all accompanied us towards Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But you don't know exactly where he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you had jumped out of the window on your own.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Without anyone's assistance; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that you named people from other people's stories, not from your own prior knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, what I lived through and what I survived will always be burned in my memory and all the people who were there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that you named them on the basis of what you heard that night, not what you had known before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people there who knew him. Not only him but each of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I am replying to you. There were people there who knew them well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Counsel has asked about your knowledge of him, not the knowledge of other people. How do you answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please clarify who "him" is referring to? I'm confused at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I precisely think about the witness, about his knowledge, not about the knowledge of other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but of whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: About Milan Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and other people who came to the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, be a little more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This knowledge of Sredoje Lukic and other men, but let us concentrate on my client, that's the knowledge that you acquired that night about Sredoje Lukic? It doesn't pre-date that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What you know about my client, Sredoje Lukic, is only from that night, not from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is a form of intimidation and even persecution of the witness. The witness extensively discussed what he knew about Sredoje Lukic. Defence counsel wants him to talk about the 14th of June. The questions put by Mr. Alarid, we are not here to persecute the witness, to make him say a number of things, but to make sure that the witness tells the truth. I would like the Trial Chamber to intervene, because the witness has stated what he knows about Sredoje Lukic. If he has doubts about other matters, then he should put his questions appropriately. As far as the knowledge of VG-38 is concerned concerning Sredoje Lukic, he told the Chamber already that he met him for the first time on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but I believe counsel is entitled to press him on -- on that. I don't see this as persecution, Mr. Ossogo. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me remind my colleague yesterday at page 83 of the transcript in response to a question from a member of the Bench about what this witness knew of Sredoje Lukic, the witness explained that he saw him every day on his way to school, and that's prior to the 14th of June, and he gave detailed descriptions of his encounters with my client prior to the 14th of June incident, and that's at page 83 of the -- yesterday's transcript. In respond to my learned friend Ossogo's question at page 81 he answered that he had seen him at the Rzav bridge because that was where the police station was. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I had indicated that you should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have already testified before this Tribunal, have you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was it in this courtroom or some other courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether it was this one or some other.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were you seated at the exact same spot as you are now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were Their Honours seated across from you as they are today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the meantime could we please have Exhibit P44, last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, just as today, prior to your testimony you were invited to read the solemn declaration that you would speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we focus from line 6 to 14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a portion of your testimony that I will read out to you since this is in English. My learned friend Mr. Domazet asked you whether you could explain how you knew those names. You explained that some individuals knew them. Did you learn their names at that very spot at that time, or was it at later date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the same space --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Pause for a moment, please. Your answer was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, again to be specific, what names are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The names are in the answer of the witness, so with your leave I would like to read it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your answer was: "There were people there who knew all four of them, and that's when we learnt their names, when they took the money and gold, whereas they knew Mitar, some of them knew Mitar from before, Milan Lukic ... they knew him from before. Milan Susnjar as well, Laco from the village, and Sredoje."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we please have a transcript reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is in front of you. This exhibit is already admitted as P44, page 1409. Testimony of this witness before the Trial Chamber in the case Prosecutor versus Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, does this not appear to you as being quite the opposite of what you've testified here yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what it is you want to state with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that your memory of the incident was much better in late 1990s, for instance, than today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not as crazy as you seem to believe I am, and I came here to state who it was who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement to the Zenica CSB, State Security Services Centre on the 11th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and 2D697 in English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] sir, did you speak the truth and nothing but the truth that time as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do we have in English also?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Meanwhile, while we're waiting for the English translation of the statement to appear, are these your personal details that we can see on the front page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll down in version in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have second page in B/C/S and fourth page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see my client's name here, Sredoje Lukic, and can you please read the statement immediately following his name, the lower portion of the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to come back to that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to take a break now. I should have said at the outset that some members of the Bench have professional duties at 1.30, and so we will adjourn at 1.30 p.m. today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we break, could I make the Court aware and the Defence aware of a scheduling problem that has as arisen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We had arranged for VG-84 to -- I'm sorry, VG-18 to testify and then VG-84 to testify at the end of the week. VG-18 has become ill this morning, so we're going to switch and do VG-84 first to give VG-18 a chance to recuperate and we expect she'll be better by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we left off talking about your 1995 statement. Can you please read out the first sentence in relation to Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the door --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Please look at the paragraph starting with "Sredoje Lukic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He allegedly --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please read out his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sredoje Lukic, he allegedly worked in the Unis wire factory." It's a very poor copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it read as follows and please listen carefully. "Sredoje Lukic, he allegedly worked in the Unis wire factory." Is this what the text says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This exhibit is already admitted under the number 1D26, so we kindly ask for admission also under --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, three years later you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] [In English] ... system exhibit number under the ERN 0300-9004. And -- thank you. Thank you very much. Could we scroll down version in English here, language, please. [Interpretation] Sir, is this your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [In English] Could we have third page in both languages. [Interpretation] Is this your signature at the bottom? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [In English] Could we have the second paragraph zoomed in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On these documents we can see the signatures and the name of this witness, which could identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So -- it's not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And I kindly request admission of those documents under the seal, also of previous statement and this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 2D4 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you read out the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Two hours after --"

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Or rather, let me read this out and you can confirm if that's exactly the text says.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: "Two hours after we arrived at the house four Serb men came, they were Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and Milan Susnjar, aka Lalko."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: "I did not know Sredoje and Milan Lukic ..." Do you recall this statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please be told where this statement was given?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Page before the last one. In English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness VG-38, I'm going to ask the registrar to display on the screen the part of the testimony you gave in the Vasiljevic case, and you will tell me whether those are the words you expressed before the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we display P44 on the screen, please, which is a transcript in the Vasiljevic case on the 1st of October, 2001, on page 1350. 1359.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I would like to read this out again in English, and it will be translated back to you because I don't have a French version. On line 17 when the question was put to you: "[In English] Can you describe to the Court how it is that you know that's the person you're referring to now is Mitar Vasiljevic?" [Interpretation] And you answered: "[In English] He used to work in Panos in the new hotel, and sometimes he would be in the Vilina Vlas Hotel." [Interpretation] And then an additional question is put to you: "[In English] Do you have any relatives that also knew him?" [Interpretation] And you answered: "Yes." This is a new question: "[In English] And without telling us the name of any relatives, can you tell us what their relationship was with Mitar Vasiljevic?" [Interpretation] And you answered: "[In English] They were on very good terms." [Interpretation] When another question was put to you [Previous translation continues] ... "[In English] that Mitar Vasiljevic worked. [Interpretation] You answered: "[In English] He was an intern there, a trainee." [Interpretation] Do you recognise that this is a statement you made and the words you uttered?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would be objecting as to the form of questioning of this witness as being highly leading. I mean, the first question is "Can you describe the Court how it was that you knew the person is Mitar Vasiljevic," and then everything else is leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Give us a specific example.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, obviously the first part "Can you describe" is an open-ended question, but as he puts his prior testimony into his head it becomes leading questioning, because I believe this would only be appropriate if this was an inconsistent answer, but this would otherwise not be proper examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What he's doing is putting to the witness the evidence from the previous trial, and you say that that is leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has not -- the witness has not stated that he could not answer the question "How did you know Mitar Vasiljevic" and I believe he's citing from this trial the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Ask the question again, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I told the witness that I would read back to him the statements he gave. After this part of his testimony was read back to him, I was asking him whether he admitted that this was right, and when I asked him whether he had testified before this Chamber and whether everything he stated was right, he said yes. So I'm just repeating this here. I believe, Your Honour, with all due respect to this judicial system, this is an international system. In the jurisdiction where I come from, namely a civil law country, when one quotes a former testimony of a witness, that is perfectly appropriate. I'm just repeating what he has already said and asking him whether this is right or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. You may go ahead. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I would also like to display page 1370, please, which is the same exhibit number, P44. On line 14. Witness VG-38, I would also like to read back to you part of the statement you gave in the Vasiljevic case. Let me repeat the questions that were put to you concerning Sredoje Lukic, and you will tell me whether this is right or not. "[In English] The person you're describing as Sredoje Lukic, did you know him prior to this day?" [Interpretation] And you answered: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... work as a police officer in Visegrad." [Interpretation] End of quote. Lines 14, 15, and 16. I have finished with this document. I would now like to display -- to display Exhibit number P51. This is a photo spread. Witness VG-38, there is a signature under one of these photographs. It is you who signed this, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Who is on this photograph you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: This photo spread was shown to you when you signed the statement which you gave to the OTP in 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, just one error in transcript page 39, line 17. I think that the quotation is "I think that he used to work as a police officer in Visegrad, I think." Those words are missing from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, have you completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, that concludes your testimony. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls VG-13. Your Honour, could I ask the Court when it intends or anticipates taking the next break? It would help in the order of questions I will put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take it 90 minutes from the time when we resumed, which was 10.50.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Judge Van Den Wyngaert is doing the arithmetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That would be 12.20? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam Witness, the Trial Chamber has ordered protective measures with respect to your testimony here. Therefore I will refer to you by your pseudonym, which is VG-13. So that the Chamber and the other members present here or the Defence attorneys and the accused present here in court will know your real name, I'm going to ask you to take a look at a sheet of paper and ask you is that your full name on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you just to sign your signature to the bottom of that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of that piece paper, we have put the name of your son. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He has also been given protective measures, so I ask during the course of your testimony you're going to refer to him to please use his pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that that pseudonym sheet be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted as P52 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-13, I'd like to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that there is an error on that information sheet related to the year when the witness is born.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May I go into private session and clarify with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-13, I'd like to begin my questions to you by asking you do you know a person by the name of Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you summarise for us just how it is that you know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I know him as a policeman. That was his job. We would come across each other on the bus and then there were also the village gatherings, dances and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to ask you about each of these different ways that you have come to know Sredoje Lukic separately, and I would like to begin by asking you questions related to --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would like to begin by asking you where is the village that you grew up in? What's the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I grew up in Jelacic village, and I got married into Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So after you were married you moved to Koritnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At what age were you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Seventeen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the village that Sredoje Lukic grew up in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Rujiste village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Chamber as best you're able how far apart are these -- is the village of Jelacici and Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The Drina River separates them but they're not far from each other. From Jelacici village there's six or seven kilometres to Rujiste, and Koritnik is even closer to Rujiste, three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the distance between Koritnik and Rujiste is three kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there a name or was there a name for this area in Visegrad that included the villages that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It was called Zupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, was it the custom in the area of Zupa for teenagers and young men and women to gather on weekends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And for what purpose would these young people gather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: To socialise, to sit around together, to eye prospective boyfriends and girlfriends.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were the gatherings confined to the members of the separate villages or was -- were members of one village often invited to the gatherings of another village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, in many villages, in the schoolhouse in Prelovo as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us if a gathering was being held in Prelovo, would the people attending it only be from Prelovo or would they be from other villages as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There would be people, young people from other villages as well. They were all looking for some merrymaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were these gatherings or these dances held on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They were held on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how would young people learn where these dances were being held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There would be posters put up on houses or lamp-posts indicating the time and place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As a teenager did you attend these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
