utterances.text: From what age did you begin attending these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Early. I started going out early around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember the age that you were, the approximate age that you were when you began to go to these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Thirteen or fourteen. Rather early, as I said, and I got married early as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately at what age did you stop going to these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: When I got married I stopped for a while, but I liked it. I found it fun to go out with my circle of friends, so I started going again, and then I stopped finally when I got employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what age were you when you got employed and stopped going to these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Twenty-four. I was 24 when I started working in the hydro engineering company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how regularly would you go to these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, we would go almost every Saturday, gatherings in various villages, so we met up quite often.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned that you -- one of the ways that you knew Sredoje Lukic was from these dances. Can you estimate for us how often you saw Sredoje Lukic at these dances?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have precise reference when we heard the answer that the witness say Sredoje Lukic was attending those parties or dances? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe it was the second question that I asked, Your Honour. Unfortunately my LiveNote is not working well and I'm not able to stop and go back and get the transcript reference but it was the second question that I asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd be happy to ask the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever see Sredoje Lukic at any of these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not saying he came often, but he did come, and we would see each other on the bus there until he bought a car to drive around town. It's a small town, so you can't help meeting people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you ever dance with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you -- did you converse with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we would meet, when he came to Huso to our village to visit or when he came to the hydro engineering company to see if there are any problems we would just say hello, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In response to Judge Robinson's question, you talked about when he would visit your village. Is this before or after he was a member of the police force in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: When he worked in the police he came with Huso, his colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that you did not see him often at these dances. Can I ask you to the best of your ability to estimate for us the frequency at which he would attend these dances? How many times a year, if that's something that you're able to do, did he attend these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Several times. He didn't come often. He had other obligations, Mr. Sredoje. He came as often as he had time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what you remember about him as a young man, his character or his personality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: He was nice. He didn't offend anybody. Life at that time was nice, and the socialising between us was good regardless of ethnicity or religion before the war, and after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now you've mentioned seeing him on a bus. Could I ask you to describe the bus service between the Zupa area and the town of Visegrad. How often did the bus run? How many different bus lines were there that serviced that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, the bus started at 6.00 to drive workers to work, at 7.30 to drive pupils to school. They could come back one at 11.00, then at 1.00 p.m., at 4.00 p.m. workers were going back from work. There was another bus at 6.00 and later, certainly, but I can't remember all these things exactly, it was such a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the same bus go to Koritnik and Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: For our village there was a van going to Gostilja and further on, and the bus went to Zupa because it was a busier line. There were more people using that line to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you say that you saw him on the bus. Can you give us some idea about how often and during what period you saw him travelling on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, he went to work and from work by bus, and later on when I got a job, too, I drove around the area, but later on I met him rather less often.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you saw him on the bus did you recognise him as the same Sredoje Lukic that you knew from these dances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've already referred to knowing him from his work as a police officer. Did you ever see Sredoje Lukic patrolling in an official capacity your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, he was a nice policeman, nice man. I can't say anything about that. He was doing his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you actually see him in your village on patrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, when he came together with Huso.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this in the village of Koritnik or in the village of Jelacici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Koritnik village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you keep referring to a person by the name of Huso. Can you tell us Huso's last name if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you lived in Koritnik, at whose house did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I lived in my own house together with my father-in-law. It was their family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you ever present when your father-in-law and Sredoje Lukic had a conversation with each other?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, what is the basis for the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What is the base for this question, Your Honour, because the witness did not mention that Sredoje Lukic knew her father-in-law. We spoke about Mr. Huso Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll ask him more broadly if Your Honour wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Put it -- you may reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did your father-in-law know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I think he did. The man had grown old in his village in Koritnik, and he visited the Omeragics and walked around Zupa and everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you ever present when Sredoje Lukic and your father-in-law exchanged words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, when they would come around for a check there would be a, "Hello, hello. Will you sit down for a coffee?" "No, we don't have time. We have to move on."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to the 14th of July, 1992, had you or any member of your family had any dispute with Sredoje Lukic or any member of his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of the company that you worked for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Hidrogradnja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that we have to redact this part of transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I discussed this with the witness. There are a sufficient number of employees in this company that she does not believe it will compromise her identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We had similar situation with VG-115, and we couldn't mention the name of company. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you briefly summarise your duties when you worked for that company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I can. I worked in the kitchen in Visegrad for six years. After that I went to work in Iraq for three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say you went to work in Iraq, are you referring to the separate country in the Middle East outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In what years were you working in Iraq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I went there in 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when did you return?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after you returned, did you have occasion to see Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Not when I came back, because I went to do fieldwork in Ugljevik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Between the time that you returned from Iraq and the 14th of June, had you ever seen Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, we saw him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that we already have answer on that question, page 51, lines from 2 up to 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, has the witness already answered that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: She's referring to another period of time she was in another part of Bosnia. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were in a place called Ugljevik. Is that a place outside of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It's between Tuzla and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did there come a time when you concluded your work there and returned to your home in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately when was it that you returned to your home in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: In 1990 I returned home. In 1991 all those things started with barricades and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Between the time that you returned to your home in Koritnik and the 14th of June, 1992, had you seen Sredoje Lukic at any occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I saw him when he came to Mujo Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When -- when did he come to Mujo Memic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: When we were locked up there to be robbed of our money and jewellery.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before I ask you questions about that day, I'd ask you to take a look around the courtroom very carefully and tell us whether you recognise the person you're describing as Sredoje Lukic in court here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection. As usual, objection related to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's noted. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe who the person is that you recognise by describing where they are sitting in the courtroom and what they are wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: To my right, he's on the right side, and to the left is Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You're looking to your left on the left side of the courtroom. There are three rows on the left side the courtroom. Which row is the person sitting in that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: He's on the right side wearing a grey suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to see any other article of clothing that he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I can see the grey suit on him, and Milan Lukic is wearing a black suit and a pink shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness has identified Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object to the exclusive and exclusionary nature and suggested nature of the idea of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, with respect to Milan Lukic, when is the first time you heard of his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, we heard him name when we came to Jusuf Memic's house, and even earlier the people who knew him better were saying that this man is wreaking havoc in Zupa, killing the people there, inflicting evil.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say earlier, can you approximate for us how much time prior to the 14th of June you first heard the name of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, we heard it from Jasmina Vila when they said that should be brought to join us in Koritnik, and other young people who went with him to school recognised him. There were some of them who even shared the same bench with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was the first time that you yourself physically saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: When he came to Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And on what date was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: 14 June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to a few days before that, the 10th of June, 1992. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you in your village that day, in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, that morning we left Koritnik village and set off towards Visegrad. That's what we had been told to do, to pack and leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to prior to when you were told to leave. Did anything happen to your village prior to being told to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, yes. On the 10th of June our village was attacked. Demands were made to turn over weapons. That's what they said. And before there was a lull in the fire, we all ran to one house, because we all had to be together, we were so afraid, women, children, and the elderly. When the fire stopped for a while we looked around to see who was dead and who was alive, and then Ilija Gavrilovic came, knocked at the door of the Kurspahic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can ask you a few more questions about the attack before we move forward. When you say "attack on the village," can you describe what actually happened to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: That's how it happened. And I thought that fire balls were falling from the sky. I don't know what they were looking for because we didn't have weapons. The people who were of military age, able-bodied, were hiding so as not to be taken away. And before that attack started, a Serb from Koritnik came. Now he must be a middle-aged, married man. He had a family, worked in Serbia. I don't know exactly which company, but at that time he was our neighbour, telling us that all the men were running into the woods because otherwise we would -- they would be taken away, whereas we women or children would be given some kind of passage to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see the people or some of the people who attacked your village on the 10th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There were some who are dead now. Those are alive are Mladjo Grujic, Milovan Jasika, Novak Simic. Then Ilija Gavrilovic and others. It was a long time ago. I can't recall it all now. I'm no longer 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see either Sredoje Lukic or Milan Lukic in your village that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Not that day. That day I didn't see either of them. Those were neighbours from our village, from Hubava, and probably from Loznica as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to the men and boys of your village during the attack or after the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They hid in a basement, and when there was a lull in the fire they ran through a valley and from there on to the woods, and then they moved to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned the names of some of the attackers. Were there other attackers that you could not see clearly or you did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, the ones I named were our neighbours. Those from Hubava village and from Loznica, I didn't see. I wasn't even able to see all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to being told that you had to leave the village. Can you please describe for the Chamber the circumstances under which you were given that directive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Milorad Lipovac, also known as Micun, from Greben village came and our next door neighbour Dusan came with him. They said we had to move. It was something like ethnic cleansing. I didn't know what ethnic was. They told us to prepare food for one or two days and we would allegedly be going to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The neighbour you've referred to as Dusan, do you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Dusan Grujic. The man is dead now. There is to reason to mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember what date -- what was the date that you were told that you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: On the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you when you were told that you had -- you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: All of us in the village gathered. An elderly lady, Kurspahic, asked him to please let us leave all of the elderly and the young, and he said that they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was this direction -- was this direction to leave given only to you or was it given to other people as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: All of the villagers. We were told that we would be going to Kladanj, to a Serb village. It was supposed to be an exchange and that they would in turn be coming over from Kladanj to live in our homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you given any instructions with respect to what you should bring with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We were only told to bring along foodstuffs for a day or two and a change of clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you believe that you would be away from your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I wasn't thinking in fact. I didn't know what a war meant. The elderly were telling us we were not coming back, whereas the young -- we, the younger generation, thought that everything was going to be resolved in a day or two and that we would be returning home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you did leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: On the 14th of June we set out from our village at 8.00. Dusan came along with a rifle in his hand, and he escorted us as far as Greben. The people were wailing. The elderly knew that they were abandoning their homes and they were weeping. So were the children. As we reached Greben two soldiers approached us. I didn't know them and I didn't dare look at them. I was sheltering my child. I was afraid of them taking away my child.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If -- I will get to what happened at Greben in a moment, but before we get that far, I would like to ask you a few more questions about what happened in Koritnik. Were you told how you would be travelling when you left Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They told us that buses would be arriving. No buses arrived. We waited from 6.00 to 8.00 in the morning. I don't know if they were deceiving us where the buses were indeed supposed to arrive or not, but in short we didn't have any transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any member of the Koritnik village that remained at this point put up any physical resistance to being evicted from their homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They weren't evicting us. We came out as Milorad Lipovac and Dusan Grujic told us to. People entrusted keys to their homes to their Serb neighbours, telling them to take care of their homes in case we returned, though there were women that I saw that immediately went round all the houses to plunder and loot them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what types of property were taken from the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They carried out TV sets, especially those that were in colour. Tractors, mills, lawn-mowers. All sorts of implements that people use to earn their living. Everything was carried away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned a few moments ago a person by the name of Jasmina Vila. Did you see her on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I saw her on the evening of the 13th of June when Stanisava Simic brought her to our village. She was supposed to join us. We didn't ask any questions. The lady brought her over and told us that she was supposed to accompany us on the following morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to observe her physical condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: She was like a peeled potato in water. She -- and you will hear witnesses who will tell you that she was raped. She was at the military camp at Kamenica for 10 days that Milan Lukic took her over there, and he was the one who brought her over to Stanisava Simic who was supposed to bring her to our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you -- you've talked about her appearing like a peeled potato in water. Could I ask you to describe with greater precision your observations about her that led you to that characterisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For example --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The lady had -- had been bitten all over her face. I didn't take the liberty to ask her about it, because I -- I was able to see that something bad had happened to her. She was black and blue, bitten all over, and that's because she was raped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how old was Jasmina Vila?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: She had completed her high school education. I don't know if she was 19 or 20. I know that she had graduated from high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, returning to the point where you were beginning to describe leaving Koritnik. You mentioned a village by the name of Greben. Where is Greben in relation to Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Off the main road linking the motorway to Zupa there's a forking off to Zupa on the right-hand side, and that's where we -- that's where we waited for the buses to arrive. They didn't arrive, however. Two soldiers appeared that I didn't know. One of them said, "Let's kill them" and the other one said, "Let's go to Prelovo first and then we'll see if we find them on our way back, if we find them there."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This incident you're describing, where did it occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Podgreben.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Milan Lukic has had his head down for the last 10 or 15 minutes. I'm not sure if it's ill or maybe the Chamber wants to inquire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you ill? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the village of Greben in relation to Koritnik, if you can tell us is it north, south, east, west?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. The transcript doesn't show that Mr. Lukic answered my question in the negative. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us where Greben was in relation to Koritnik in terms of whether it was north, south, east or west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It lies in the same direction. One goes through the village of Greben and then turns right to our village, the village of Koritnik. It -- it's in the same direction alongside the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is Greben on the way -- or is Greben in between Koritnik and Visegrad town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described what happened in Greben. Was there any other event that occurred while you travelled down to Visegrad town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Between Greben and Banja we were taken over by Milorad Lipovac, aka Micun. He took charge of us. He took a rifle and said, "I'll escort you to Banja, seeing that there are no buses."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did anything occur after meeting him while he was escorting you down to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: People were weeping and crying. They didn't know where they were headed. We proceeded along the road to Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you reached an area known as Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did anything occur there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We passed through the village of Sase and reach the intersection where one turns off to Vilina Vlas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did anything happen in the area of that intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Two soldiers approached us from the direction of Vilina Vlas. They had black paint smeared over their faces. I didn't dare ask who they were. Micun spoke to one individual called Crni. I don't know his name. He said, "You are not supposed to touch them over here, and I don't know what's going to happen over there."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when he referred to over there, where did you believe he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: He meant what was going to happen to us as we reached Visegrad, I think most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you did reach the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. There was drizzling rain. They told us -- Mico told us that we should go to the Red Cross office. Somebody was probably going to receive us there and take -- organise transportation to Kladanj. We received -- we arrived in that particular street. It was a Sunday. The shops were closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It may have been around 3.00. We were proceeding on foot and the children and the elderly weren't able to walk fast. I didn't have a watch on me so I can't tell you the precise time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would I be correct in saying that the path you followed from Koritnik, the road you travelled from Koritnik to Visegrad town was roughly on the eastern bank of the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: On the right bank of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you actually go to the Red Cross office in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We did. Since the Red Cross office wasn't opened, we went on to an area in front of the new hotel, under a tree to shelter ourselves from the rain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the new hotel in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: On the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is it with respect to the old bridge, the Stari Most bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It's before one reaches the old bridge -- or, rather, it's beyond the bridge. You have first the bridge and then the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was the Red Cross office with respect to the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The Jondza street beyond the new hotel. It wasn't very far off.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe the area in front of the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It was a street. There was an area that was stone flagged. There was a poplar tree and a garden. There were benches one could sit on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you were -- did the entire group from Koritnik arrive at the new hotel at the same time you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. We all arrived at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While you were in front of the new hotel did you see any men in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They had multicoloured camouflage uniforms, and they had rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell what organisation they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: They most probably belonged to an army, but I wouldn't be able to tell you which one. They didn't have any head-wear. They didn't have any caps that could identify their membership.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did -- did the group remain in front of the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Less than an hour. Mitar Vasiljevic arrived next and told us to -- to move over to Memic's house, Mujo Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time the group was in front of the new hotel did you see any police officers there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There were soldiers and policemen, some seven to eight men. They had grey uniforms. They had caps, and they had some insignia on their arms, on their sleeves, and on their caps, but I wouldn't be able to tell you what sort of insignia that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. You've just testified that Mitar Vasiljevic arrived and told the group to move to the Memic house, Mujo Memic's house. Approximately what time of the day was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Half past 3.00 or 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of what area in the town you were to go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We knew that Jusuf Memic resided on Pionirska Street, opposite the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's the name of that school building, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I think it was called Petar Kocic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the area that the school was in and Pionirska Street was in, did that part of town have a particular name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Nova Mahala, and the street was called Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the entire group go up to the Nova Mahala area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the group go up alone or was it escorted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Somebody shouted out that Mitar Vasiljevic had been escorting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I ask the registrar to prepare 65 ter 18. It's a photograph. I know it takes a while to load up. I'll be using it in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did it take the group to arrive at Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We had to cross the Rzava bridge. It took the elderly perhaps some 20 minutes to cross that distance, and that included all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was the police station in relation to the path or the route that the group took between the new hotel and the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The police station was to the right from the Rzava bridge. One would turn right to go to the police station immediately after crossing the Rzava bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at Pionirska Street what did -- what did you and other members of the group do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Some entered Jusuf Memic's house. Others went into Mujo Memic's house. Mujo Memic was Jusuf's son and the two houses were one next to the other. On our way there we came across several women. I don't know who they were. They were going in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you to take a look at 65 ter number 18 and ask you is it on the screen in front of you? Can you see a photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recognise the area that's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher to assist you making some markings on this photograph, and the first marking -- and the first marking I'm going to ask you to make is would you write "VG-13" on the bottom of the photograph so that we know the markings were made by you. Just somewhere down on the border of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Right here?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned two houses so far, Jusuf Memic's house and Mujo Memic's house. Could I ask you to put a "JM" to show us where Jusuf Memic's house was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to please put an "MM" on the house or the roof of the house of Mujo Memic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you about a fire that took place in this area later that day. Before I do that, do you know the name of the person who owned the house where the fire occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Adem Omeragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to put an "AO" to indicate the place where the fire took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, could I ask you to draw an arrow indicating the path that the group took as it arrived into this area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to draw an arrow to indicate the direction that the group was walking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And there's no need to make a mark, but the large building on the right of this photograph and what appears to be a large yard in front of it, is this the school that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. That's the school building, and this is the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender 65 ter number 18 or the version marked up by VG-13 as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's admitted as P53 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-13, before I ask you to describe what occurred that afternoon, I'm going to show you a computer programme that has a 360-degree view of this area, and I'm going to ask you to orient the Chamber to the -- the relevant buildings and objects that we can see prior to telling us about what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the feed from the Prosecutor be put up. And, Your Honour, this was 65 ter Exhibit 175 that I would like to now show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we are just coming up to the time for the break, so it may be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, you should be able to see on your screen now an image of an aerial view of the Visegrad area with several locations marked. This is the 360 degree programme as we've been referring to it and it's 65 ter 175. Perhaps the Court will find it helpful if I just give some brief instruction about how it is to work. I'm going to ask the witness to look at pictures from Pionirska Street, so all anyone who wants to use this programme needs to do is place the cursor over the label Pionirska Street and click on that. I'd ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to do that now. It zooms in on Pionirska Street. I'm going to ask him to zoom in again by clicking on Pionirska Street and here's an aerial view of the location. I'm going to ask him once again zoom in by clicking on the location, and we are now in the backyard of the Memic houses. Before asking the witness to comment on what we're looking at I'm going to ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to just take a view around the yard and then I will ask the witness to tell us what we are viewing. So, Mr. Van Hooydonk, if you could just move slowly around so that the Chamber and all those present in the courtroom can get a sense of the location. And if we could stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-13, do you recognise the location depicted in this photograph that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Unfortunately I'm not able to have you mark this, but I will be showing you stills from this image and ask you to mark them later on in your testimony. The two houses that we can -- or two house that is we can see in the mid-ground of that picture, do you recognise those houses? There's a white one on the right and a yellow one on the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Some of this was built later. This here is Jusuf Memic's house and this entranceway was added later. The one up there is Mujo Memic's house. This was built later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We're not able to see your -- where you're pointing to, so if I could ask you to describe the house of Jusuf Memic by telling us the colour of it and where it is in the picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Jusuf Memic's house is the one on the right in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What colour is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It has something like an awning, small roof in the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what colour is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: White. White, covered with tiles. The entrance is on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The -- can you see a part of the Mujo Memic house in this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It's behind the newly built one, yellowish facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that we move or pan to the left. And, Your Honours, I appreciate that the record is not going to be terribly useful without the witness marking and that's why towards the end of her testimony I will ask her to make some markings on stills taken from this programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We are now looking at a house that is partially destroyed and is obviously not being inhabited at the moment. Do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what do you recognise this house to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It's Adem Omeragic's house. It has been destroyed, burnt. We were burnt, too, in the lower part of that house. It's overgrown now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, to demonstrate how the programme works I'm going to ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to click on the door on the lower level and as you can see, we zoom in and I'll ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to do that again and then we are actually in the room. So if we could back out of the room, please. And if we could pan to the left once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This area behind the Adem Omeragic house -- if we could stop there and perhaps even move a little bit to the right. What is this area that we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It's so-called Glavica neighbourhood in Visegrad, and this is a little brook near Adem Omeragic's house carrying waste waters and sludge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So between the Glavica neighbourhood and the Adem Omeragic house there's a small brook that waste water runs down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've spoken to both my colleagues on the Defence about the admission of this exhibit. They have not had a chance to fully examine the exhibit but will do that tonight and tomorrow we'll discuss the possibility of perhaps admitting the document or the evidence on consent. Because the programme deals with many locations that this witness will not be testifying about, I feel it might be inappropriate to be tendering it without having the proper foundation with respect to the other aspects of the programme, but I anticipate that tomorrow perhaps there will be agreement on the admission of the document so I'd simply ask that it be marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will become Exhibit P54 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG-13, I want to return to where we left off. You talked about arriving in this neighbourhood. Which of the two houses did you go to initially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: First of all, we went to Jusuf Memic's house, then we went to Mujo Memic's house, some of us, to kind of relieve one house because there were too many of us. And we also changed our clothes, those who had a change of clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when someone came to the houses who you recognised and addressed a member of the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic came.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately what time did Mitar Vasiljevic arrive at the Memic house -- houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, it was 5.00. We did not have a clock. We had to try to determine the time approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you -- can you describe for us how did you know this person's name was Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I knew him as a waiter. He worked in Novi Hotel, sometimes in Panos. He waited at my table sometime when I came back from fieldwork to get a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When he came to the Memic houses, did he have a conversation with one of the members of the group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: He approached Mujo Halilovic, gave him a piece of paper with something written on it to the effect that we need not be afraid, that nobody would do us any harm. He took out a small bottle, a half litre bottle, perhaps, and said, "Will you have a drink, Mujo?" And Mujo said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just to clarify your last answer, who -- what's the name of the person who gave the other person a piece of paper? It's unclear who gave the paper to whom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic gave Mujo Halilovic a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that he took out a small bottle. Who is the person who took out the small bottle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see what was written on that paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I didn't read it myself, but we were close by, and other people asked Mujo, asked what was written, and he said, "Don't worry. No need to be afraid. No harm will come to us." I couldn't see what was written myself but I could see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did Mitar Vasiljevic remain at the Memic houses at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Not long. He left soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was there a reference to a protected witness at line 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There is a witness with -- no, there wasn't, Your Honour. This was one of the victims in the fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after Mitar Vasiljevic left that some men in the Koritnik group were taken from the house to do some work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. Men in camouflage uniforms came to take people and bury them in Strajiste cemetery. Medo Kurspahic, Edhem, Redzo Memisevic, Osman Kurspahic. Some of them went to Nezluk to bury somebody, I don't know who, and those who went to Strajiste, when they came back I asked them whom they had buried. They said Alija, who worked at the petrol station. I don't know the last name. And Alija's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time later in the day when several other men came to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Later when those people came back from that errand they started crying. They said, "Nothing will save us now. We'll never get back home. We'll never get back anywhere," and then they fell silent. Milan Lukic armed with a rifle came to the door. Milan Susnjar came, nicknamed Lace, and they told us to move all of us into one room. We who had come from Mujo's house came to see those people who had come from the burial to learn what was going to become of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time how many people are with Milan Lukic when he arrives at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There was Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic was somewhere around the house. He was seen. There was Bosko Djuric, because Edhem said earlier those who can, jump out of the window and then after he leaned out of the window he turned back in and said, "Don't even try jumping out. There are some more of them around the house. They're watching."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Was Mitar Vasiljevic present at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if you're able, approximately what time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It was perhaps 6.00 when it was all happening, when they came to take our money and our gold and strip us naked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, can I ask you to describe what happened when -- when these men arrived at the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We all crammed ourselves into one room. Milan Lukic threw a rag on the table and said, "Put all your money and your jewellery here. If after that we find something else on you, you get a bullet in the head," and indeed later they stripped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before we get to this -- that part of your evidence, when you describe being gathered into a room, do you know what room of the house it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: At Jusuf Memic's house the room facing the street on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you've referred to a table in the room. Can you describe that table? How large was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Almost like the one in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's the same approximate size of the witness -- the witness desk that you're at here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at the time that Milan Lukic places the -- what you've described as a rag on the table, where are you precisely in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We were all, as I said, in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Recognising that there were many people in the room, I'm asking you just to confine yourself to where were you yourself in the room in relation to the table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I wasn't close to the table, but on the other hand we couldn't have been far. We were all crammed in there. Perhaps a metre or two away from the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall if there were lights on in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: No. We didn't think to turn the lights on because it was still light outside. It was a summer day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any difficulty seeing his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There was no difficulty in seeing him. How could we not see each other, being in the same room?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have anything disguising his face such as a mask or face paint or anything that would have disguised his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the members of the group put their valuables and their money on the rag that Milan Lukic laid out on the table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Anyone who had anything, who had taken something from home turned it all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did this -- did the property include watches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What property belonging to you did you place on the table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: At that time I had come back recently from Iraq. I had Deutschmarks, dinars and gold. I turned everything over to them. If only they had at least released me as they should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the members of the Koritnik group placed their belongings on the rag on that table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Later on Mitar Vasiljevic turned up too. They put everything in one bag and Milan Lukic told Mitar Vasiljevic to take us to drink.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's correction: Said, "Let's go drinking now."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier about being searched for property. When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: It was around 6.00 when they came to take away the money and the gold. After that Milan Susnjar took us to the adjacent room to strip us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you please tell us what happened in that adjacent room with Milan Susnjar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: He was sitting at a desk, and as we were coming in we had to remove all our clothes, remaining completely naked. We had to dance. Of course they were insulting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were children made to take their clothes off as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. Mothers had to remove all the clothes for -- from small children as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there one young woman who refused to remove her clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes, there was, a young woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Two women had to tear the clothes off her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this -- this stripping of the people from Koritnik and the taking of their property take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: All this went on until perhaps 8.00 or 9.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you were beginning to mention about someone saying -- or Mitar Vasiljevic saying something about going for a drink. Can I ask you to describe what happened when the suggestion was made to go get a drink? Did they leave the location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The rest of us stayed there wondering what was to become of us while they left, Mitar Vasiljevic and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's very important in your testimony that you precisely identify who is where at what time and what they are doing. So rather than simply say "the others," could I ask you to actually call the names even though it may seem repetitious to you, to call the names of the people and tell us what they were doing. When you say "others," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, Susnjar, nicknamed Laco, Milan, Bosko Djuric. Of course all of them went away together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Sredoje Lukic at the point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic was around the house, and of course at that time he probably went off with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "around the house, "do you mean inside or outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when some of the younger women were removed from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milan Lukic took out Jasmina Vila twice that night. Ms. Kurspahic and Mujesira was also taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you if you know the first name and the family name of each of the women. You've told us Jasmina Vila. Could you tell us the first name and the family name of the other two women if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Ifeta Kurspahic, the wife of Dzevad Kurspahic. Mujesira Kurspahic, the wife of another Kurspahic, Eniz.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the approximate age of these women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I don't know. Twenty. Mujesira was perhaps 23. Ifeta Kurspahic had been married to her husband for just 11 months at the time. She was young. Jasmina Vila had just completed secondary school, 20-ish.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when they were returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately for how long were they away from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: An hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When they returned can you describe their appearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The clothes on them were the same, only the faces had changed. We asked them what had happened. They wouldn't say anything, neither Ifeta nor Mujesira, and Jasmina Vila only asked for a pill to treat her headache.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you and the other women there come to the belief that they had been sexually assaulted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Their faces were completely changed, but they wouldn't say anything, and we didn't -- wanted to ask anything seeing how their clothes were put on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At some point after the young women returned to the house did you become aware that the -- some of the men who had been there earlier had returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I ask you to tell us who it was who returned to the house, using their full name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Out of the men from our group or the soldiers? Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The soldiers who you've referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic came together with them into the room. He brought them there. He left them. Later he left, and we stayed perhaps until 11.00 in Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say Milan Lukic brought them there, when you say "them," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I mean Jasmina Vila, Ifeta Kurspahic, and Mujesira Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After that point in time did any of the men who were there earlier in the evening return to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the women returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Well, Jasmina Vila took a pill and sort of lay down. We others sat around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Later on they came to take us from Jusuf Memic's house to Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "they," can I ask you to once again list the full names of all the people you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic, and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any others present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: I didn't see the others because we were going down the stairs. There was no time to see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you saying that there were others there that you did not -- were not able to see clearly enough to recognise or that you don't know if there was any more than three present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There were others, but we didn't dare to look at them and find out whether they were soldiers or civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were moved from the Memic house to the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe how you were moved from the Memic house to the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic came and knocked at the door. He had a rifle. The children were asleep. The elderly were seated. We got up and went toward the staircase, and we were told that we should go and pack up and move to a different house since we were not safe in that one. We started packing and preparing to leave. We had to. We were ordered to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who told you that you should pick up and move to a different house and that you were not safe in the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you and the other members of the Koritnik group follow his directions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: We started descending the stairs. Mr. Lukic was standing at the doorway and yelling at us, "Faster, faster." Kada Sehic, the wife of Rasim Sehic, approached him and asked him to be allowed to put her shoes on. He replied, "You won't need them. Move faster." In the group that was following me one of the older men shouted, "Is that one of our neighbours, Milan Lukic? Yes. He took my husband Rasim and my son called Kender." He replied, "Stop talking and keep moving." Thus we went down the stairs and headed for Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified that Milan Lukic was standing by a doorway, I believe. Did you have to pass through at that doorway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And at the time that you passed through that doorway were you close enough that if you wanted to touch Milan Lukic you could?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you if you're able to approximate the distance that you were from Milan Lukic as you passed through the doorway he was standing by.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: The door was opened and the distance that we were passing was less than 30 centimetres. It was really close.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see him as you passed through the doorway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where Sredoje Lukic was at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: As we set out for Adem Omeragic's house, Edhem shouted that we were followed by Sredoje Lukic, that he was walking alongside us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time is it still daylight out or has it become dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Of course it was dark. It must have been around 11.00 p.m. when we were forced to move to Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there lights on in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: There were no lights.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Which house are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: Adem Omeragic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the Memic house as you were leaving were there lights on in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-13
utterances.text: No, there weren't any. The lights were on in the neighbourhood but not in Mr. Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we'll have to take the break now and we resume in the morning at 8.50 a.m.
